process.title: Implement bell.py (Bell numbers) with tests
process.scope: Owns only the new files bell.py and tests/test_bell.py. Does not touch any existing file, does not implement tapcode or decimaltime, does not import from other modules.
process.task:
Implement bell.py with the function `bell_number(n: int) -> int` that returns the n-th Bell number B_n (the number of partitions of an n-element set), with the convention B_0 = 1. Use only the Python standard library. Do not import tapcode or decimaltime.

Validation rules (exact):
- n must be an int; bool is rejected (bool is not acceptable even though it subclasses int): bell_number(True) raises TypeError.
- Non-int inputs raise TypeError: bell_number(2.5) raises TypeError, bell_number("5") raises TypeError.
- Negative n raises ValueError: bell_number(-1) raises ValueError.

Acceptance examples — every one of these must have a corresponding test case in tests/test_bell.py (逐字 transcribed from the work order):
- bell_number(0) == 1
- bell_number(1) == 1
- bell_number(2) == 2
- bell_number(3) == 5
- bell_number(4) == 15
- bell_number(5) == 52
- bell_number(6) == 203
- bell_number(7) == 877
- bell_number(8) == 4140
- bell_number(9) == 21147
- bell_number(10) == 115975
- bell_number(15) == 1382958545
- bell_number(20) == 51724158235372
- bell_number(-1) raises ValueError
- bell_number(2.5), bell_number("5"), bell_number(True) each raise TypeError

Constraints: only create bell.py and tests/test_bell.py (both new files); do not modify any existing file; standard library only.

Checks (run from repository root, verbatim from work order): python3 -m pytest tests/test_bell.py -q and python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
